value.answer: Short term, at low doses (5 mg or less a day), it looks safe for most adults. Common side effects are headache and grogginess, and they go away when you stop. Long term is less clear. A preliminary study presented to the American Heart Association in November 2025 linked a year or more of use in adults with insomnia to higher heart failure rates, but it can't prove cause and hasn't been peer-reviewed. A later 2026 analysis reportedly found no significant link, so it's still open. Doctors generally don't want it used long term without a good reason. It can also interact with blood thinners and antidepressants, so check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take either.
